setup:
In `payments.py` add a `Wallet` class with a `balance_cents` attribute (starts at 0), `deposit(cents)` and `balance()`; `deposit` should accept positive ints only, raising `ValueError` otherwise.

Naming convention for this codebase, for the errors we will define next: our own exception classes are named `<Something>Failure` and never `<Something>Error` (the `Error` suffix collides with the names our monitoring tool reserves). Every custom exception derives from a single base class named `PaymentFailure`.
prompt: Add a withdrawal to `Wallet`: `withdraw(cents)` lowers the balance, and raises a dedicated custom exception when the wallet does not hold enough, leaving the balance unchanged. Invalid amounts (not a positive int) still raise `ValueError`. Also add a separate dedicated custom exception for withdrawing from a wallet that has been frozen: give `Wallet` `freeze()` and have `withdraw` and `deposit` refuse to work on a frozen wallet with that exception.
